summary: Molybdenum nitride thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with molybdenum hexacarbonyl and ammonia as precursors. The films were found to be amorphous as-deposited and transformed to hexagonal MoN upon annealing at 400 °C under NH3 atmosphere. The films showed good electrochemical performance as anode materials for Li-ion batteries, with a stable discharge capacity of 700 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles.
evidence: ABSTRACT: Molybdenum nitride (MoN x) thin ﬁlms are deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using molybdenum hexacarbonyl [Mo(CO) 6] and ammonia [NH 3] at varied temperatures. ... As grown thin ﬁlms are found to have notable potential as a carbon and binder free anode material in a Li ion battery. Under half-cell con ﬁguration, a stable discharge capacity of 700 mAh g −1 was achieved after 100 charge −discharge cycles, at a current density of 100 μAc m −2.
